video.title: A New AI Gold Rush Just Started. Don’t Miss This One. (+4 Ideas)

summary: Koerner Office episode where host Chris Koerner and guest Cody pitch four to five digital business ideas. The main one is an AI-avatar UGC ad creative agency for supplement e-commerce brands, followed by a Reddit/Perplexity pain-point research method illustrated with med spa lead generation, a webinar-to-ebook lead magnet service, a city-specific cheap flight deals newsletter (an unbundled Going/Scott's Cheap Flights), and Nextdoor before/after marketing for lawn care. Most figures are hypothetical projections or hearsay; the key takeaway is to pick a niche with budgets, offer a done-for-you deliverable, and use AI for production while the human curates.

speakers.name: Cody
speakers.description: Operator with AI automation and agency experience; formerly ran webinars at Rupa Health; active on LinkedIn and Twitter

ideas.name: AI avatar UGC ad creative agency for supplement brands
ideas.one_liner: Productised weekly delivery of AI-avatar UGC video ads (avatars holding the product) to supplement e-commerce brands.
ideas.business_model: Monthly retainer for a fixed weekly volume of ad creatives
ideas.customer: Supplement e-commerce brands that already spend heavily on Facebook/Meta ads (often ~$10M/yr revenue with ~5 staff)
ideas.problem: Brands need to test hundreds of ad creatives monthly; human UGC creators are slow, costly (~$100/video), give one script variation and require shipping product.
ideas.offer: 25 AI-avatar UGC videos per week, with hook research, scripts and edits, informed by a performance dashboard; next batch based on top performers. Does not run the ads.

price_points.label: what some agencies reportedly charge for 10 videos

pricing.notes: Claimed that 16 clients at $5k/month gives about $80k/month.

acquisition_channels.details: Find supplement e-com brands, identify the founders, email all ~5 staff with a Google Drive folder of 5 sample ads made for them, backed by pain-point research.

quote.text: Cool, I made you some ads. Here's here's five examples of the ads that I can make for you.
quote.speaker: Cody

ideas.delivery: Operator uses AI tools (e.g. MakeUGC.ai, n8n/make.com workflows) to research pain points, write scripts, generate about 50 videos, curates the best 25 plus ~5 bonus. Client's own creators can remake winners.
unit_economics_claims: 25 ads can be made in ~2 hours, ~32 hours/week for 16 clients
Search volume for AI UGC rose from 1,600 to 4,300/month in a year

acquisition.how: Cold email to limited companies is PECR-legal; agents can find brands, generate sample ads and send; human handles replies and sales calls.

onboarding.how: Needs brand brief, product photos and dashboard access; mostly templated but needs human input.

delivery.how: Agents can research, script and generate videos; human curates winners weekly.

support.how: Weekly client feedback and performance-based iteration needs human judgement.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in UK; cold email to Ltd companies is OK. Supplements carry ASA/CAP health-claim rules and AI avatar disclosure considerations. Target UK or US brands remotely.

risks: Platform-compliance risk: Meta and ASA rules on health claims in supplement ads
AI avatar tool quality, cost and policy changes; commoditisation as more agencies copy
Revenue depends on client creative performance and churn when ads go stale
Hours claim is optimistic for 16 clients

ideas.name: Reddit/AI pain-point research to build niche lead gen (med spa example)
ideas.one_liner: Use Perplexity/ChatGPT deep research on Reddit to find an industry's pain points, then sell lead gen or related services; med spas shown as example.
ideas.business_model: Pay-per-customer or retainer lead generation for med spas
ideas.problem: Over-reliance on discount platforms like Groupon yielding poor customers; client acquisition and retention.
ideas.offer: Find new paying customers for med spas (e.g. $300 per new customer found) via Facebook ads to affluent women 30-50 and Google Maps/local SEO optimisation.

pricing.model: Pay per acquired customer or retainer

price_points.label: example cost to med spa vs ~$5k LTV

pricing.notes: Med spa lead LTV estimated ~$5,000 (4-8 visits/yr).

acquisition_channels.details: Outreach with subject like 'Are you sick of relying on Groupon too much?' tailored from scraped complaints; guessed 20% response rate.

quote.text: Groupon gets you terrible customers. I get you good customers. Like, there's literally your subject line. You probably get a 20% response rate
quote.speaker: Cody

ideas.delivery: Facebook ads targeting affluent women 30-50, Google Maps listing optimisation (keywords, photos, directory citations), possibly white-labelled tooling such as GoHighLevel.

acquisition.how: Cold email to limited-company med spas is legal; tailored copy via AI.

onboarding.how: Ad accounts and listing access required.

delivery.how: Ads and local SEO partly tool-driven but need oversight.

support.how: Client reporting and lead quality disputes.

uk_applicability.notes: UK med spas/aesthetic clinics exist; advertising of prescription-only treatments (e.g. Botox) is restricted by ASA/MHRA; Groupon exists in UK.

quotes.text: building a business is easy once you know a thing that people hate doing and you come in and be like, you pay me, I do the thing you hate.
quotes.speaker: Cody

ideas.name: Webinar-to-ebook lead magnet service
ideas.one_liner: Turn B2B companies' webinar transcripts into branded ebooks/lead magnets for LinkedIn comment-to-download campaigns.
ideas.customer: B2B marketers at companies running webinars
ideas.problem: Companies run webinars but lack time to repurpose them into lead magnets and grow email lists.
ideas.offer: Convert each webinar into an ebook PDF, LinkedIn post and lead magnet flow that grows the email list for future webinars.

price_points.label: example price; half price if client lets you pitch their email list

pricing.notes: Also suggested halving price in exchange for access to the client's webinar sign-up list.

acquisition_channels.details: Find low-view webinars on YouTube (filter this week, over 20 min), find company marketers on Apollo, email with a free sample ebook made from their webinar.

quote.text: Hey, I turn webinars into ebooks for lead magnets for LinkedIn. Is that interesting?
quote.speaker: Cody

acquisition_channels.details: DM marketers with a free ebook from their last webinar. Note: individual DMs may be PECR-sensitive.

ideas.delivery: Take webinar transcript, have Claude write an ebook, design in Canva, deliver; LinkedIn comment-guide automation via Phantom Buster or VAs.

acquisition.how: Finding webinars and emailing company marketers can be automated; B2B corporate emails are legal; LinkedIn DMs less so.

delivery.how: Transcript to LLM to ebook with brand template; light human review.

support.how: Revisions via agent with occasional human.

uk_applicability.notes: B2B webinars are common in the UK; cold email to company addresses is allowed under PECR.

risks: Webinar owners may not want to share content or branding

quotes.speaker: Cody

quotes.text: Over 60% of B2B businesses run a webinar every month

ideas.name: City-specific cheap flight deals newsletter
ideas.one_liner: Local-airport flight deal subscription (e.g. Dallas flights) built from Google Flights alerts and rewritten with AI, an unbundled Going.com.
ideas.business_model: Subscription plus affiliate kickbacks and newsletter ad slots
ideas.customer: Travellers in a specific city who want cheap flights from their home airport
ideas.problem: Generic deal newsletters feature flights from elsewhere, not from the subscriber's city.
ideas.offer: Email alerts of cheap flights from one city, with the best deals gated behind a paid yearly subscription.

pricing.notes: Yearly preferred to reduce churn; refund if you don't fly, assuming few claim.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ads to a signup form or Beehiiv landing page.
Domain like dallasflights.com ($11 on Namecheap) ranks easily for the city phrase.

ideas.delivery: Set Google Flights price tracking emails for each route from a city, forward to a listener that rewrites into newsletter via AI with links, send to subscribers.
ideas.startup_cost: About $11 domain; set up in a weekend

acquisition.how: Paid ads and SEO are inbound and automatable.

delivery.how: Alert email to AI rewrite to send; occasional review.

uk_applicability.notes: Works from UK airports (London, Manchester); Google Flights alerts work; scraping/ToS and affiliate travel rules and ATOL-type issues if selling bookings.

risks: Google Flights alerts may breach ToS if scraped at scale
Refund guarantee may cost more than expected

ideas.name: Nextdoor before/after lawn care marketing
ideas.one_liner: Lawn care business that wins customers only through organic Nextdoor before-and-after posts in the neighbourhood.
ideas.problem: Homeowners want trusted local lawn services.
ideas.offer: Lawn care with before/after posts naming the street; possibly a free first job.

acquisition_channels.details: Post before/after photos on Nextdoor for each job, e.g. 'I just did X house in your neighborhood'; door knock offering a free lawn for the first post.

quote.text: He does lawn care in a neighborhood and he does before and after pictures. It's all he does.
quote.speaker: Cody

ideas.delivery: Physical lawn mowing by the operator.
unit_economics_claims: Idea of making $50k in a summer (hypothetical)

acquisition.how: Photos and posts need the operator on site; door knocking is in-person.

uk_applicability.notes: Nextdoor exists in UK with smaller reach; gardening seasonal; works similarly with local Facebook groups.

tactics.name: Sample-first cold email with ready-made ads
steps: List supplement e-commerce brands
Identify all ~5 staff/founders
Research customer pain points
Create 5 sample ads in a Google Drive folder
Email the folder link offering hundreds of ads a month

quote.text: You just open this Google Drive folder. You're going to see five ads of the of the hundred that I can make.
quote.speaker: Cody

tactics.name: Reddit-quote scripting for niche products
steps: Pick a very narrow niche (e.g. creatine gummies for women long-distance runners)
Ask Perplexity/ChatGPT for pain points and Reddit quotes
Build hooks and scripts from the quotes
Generate videos

tactics.name: Pain-point mining via Reddit deep research
steps: Prompt Perplexity: main pain points for [industry] Reddit
Pick a pain point you can solve
Drill down with ChatGPT deep research on complaints across Reddit, Instagram, Facebook groups
Craft cold outreach that names the pain
Check demand on Google Trends

tactics.name: Copy the leading competitor via layered deep research
steps: Find 5 businesses crushing it in the niche
Pick the best
Run new deep research prompts on its growth, pricing history and fulfilment
Copy the playbook

tactics.name: Local SEO via consistent directory listings
steps: Build Google Business Profile with keywords, services and interior photos
Submit identical name/address/phone to Yelp, Foursquare, MapQuest
Aim for Google Maps pack top 3

tactics.name: Find prospects via low-view YouTube webinars
steps: Search YouTube for webinar, filter this week and over 20 minutes
Ignore view counts
Find company marketers on Apollo
Cold email with a free ebook from their webinar

tactics.name: Pricing hack: half price for list access
steps: Quote e.g. $2,000/month
Offer $1,000/month if you may pitch their webinar signups
Gain customers through customers

tactics.name: Annual plan with a refund guarantee
steps: Offer yearly membership (~$72)
Guarantee a refund if they don't fly with you within a year
Few will claim

tactics.name: Niche down within an industry
steps: Pick a vertical (biotech, cybersecurity)
Reference case-study names known in that category in outreach

warnings.warning: Ad creatives go stale in about two months, so winners need constant replacement.

quote.text: it's going to be stale in two months.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't pitch businesses that don't run ads; target those already addicted to ads.

quote.text: you want to find people that already know that ads work and offer them something better.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Posting before/after jobs you didn't do is dishonest; do it ethically.

lessons.lesson: Sell to buyers who already spend heavily on the thing you improve instead of convincing non-buyers.
Unsexy, boring B2B niches (webinars) often have budgets and little competition.

quote.text: the more unsexy the thing is and like the more like not cool it is that is where you just
quote.speaker: Cody

lessons.lesson: Sell a narrow done-for-you deliverable on a recurring cadence rather than running the client's whole channel.
Use AI for production and keep the human as curator who picks winners.

quote.text: The job of the human is like you're just a curator. You're just like picking the winners.
quote.speaker: Cody

lessons.lesson: Copy proven pricing models and unbundle big players by going local or niche.
Do the work upfront (free samples) so outreach shows value and validates demand.
Check market growth with Google Trends before launching a lead-gen business.
Clients who can do it themselves still pay for time saved; the DIY risk is small.
Do the simple thing fast, e.g. buy the domain, instead of over-planning.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly brainstormed ideas with hypothetical math and no first-hand results for the businesses pitched; some public revenue figures (Going.com) quoted from a quick search. Guest's anecdotes (Rupa Health, $100/video) are first-hand but peripheral.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells the TK Owners community; sponsor reads for get.online domains and Graph.
